To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of EVs is not necessarily a carbon abatement strategy.
the carbon intensity of electricity consumption for plug in hybrid EV charging is strongly influenced by the temporal alignment between EV charging and electricity sector emission intensity.
the use of EVs can lead to reductions in carbon emissions, but the magnitude of those reductions depends on the electricity generation mix.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to achieve a low carbon transport system, and how to achieve a sustainable transport system, and the two may not be the same.

the development of a new approach for assessing the potential of electric vehicles (EVs), and plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) in particular, in the context of a low carbon electricity sector.
understanding the potential for EVs to reduce carbon emissions from the transport sector.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EVs will not deliver abatement if electricity generation is not decarbonized.
EVs can be a significant part of a low carbon mobility solution, but only if they are used with a clean energy mix and with careful charging management.

EVs can reduce carbon emissions, but only if the electricity supply is also low carbon, and that may require some significant investment in renewable energy generation and transmission infrastructure, as well as the provision of charging infrastructure and management strategies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EVs are not a magic solution for carbon emissions reduction, but that they are part of an integrated package of measures.
there are a range of possible carbon abatement outcomes depending on the power system integration scenario, the emissions accounting approach, and the electricity mix.
the potential benefits from the implementation of a low carbon mobility strategy are substantial, but there is no one size fits all approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many ways to integrate EVs into the electricity system, and each has a different impact on GHG emissions, so a range of options must be considered.
the carbon emissions from EVs will vary substantially depending on the electricity system in which they are charged.
the emissions from the electricity sector will need to be substantially reduced in order for EV use to deliver significant GHG abatement.
